config.title: Objects, Prototypes & Classes

intro.title: Objects, Prototypes & Classes
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple program to manage a collection of books, each represented as an object with properties like title and author. You will learn how to create and manipulate JavaScript objects, which are fundamental data structures for storing key-value pairs. The lesson will then introduce prototypes to share methods between objects efficiently, and finally, you will use modern ES6 classes to create object blueprints with constructors and methods. By the end, you'll understand how objects, prototypes, and classes work together to organize code in JavaScript.
intro.usecase: Objects, prototypes, and classes are fundamental to organizing data and behavior in modern web applications. You'll use these concepts when building user profile systems where each user is an object instance with properties like name and email, and methods for updating preferences. In e-commerce applications, product catalogs use class-based structures to manage items with shared characteristics like price calculations and inventory tracking. Dashboard components often inherit from base UI classes to maintain consistent styling and behavior across charts, tables, and control panels.

objectives: Construct JavaScript objects using both literal syntax and constructor functions
Manipulate object properties by adding, updating, and deleting key-value pairs
Implement inheritance by linking objects through prototype chains
Configure class definitions with constructors, methods, and static properties
Initialize class instances and apply inheritance using the 'extends' keyword
Integrate prototype methods to extend functionality across multiple objects
Control object behavior through property descriptors and accessor methods

steps.title: Create a basic object literal
steps.instruction: Create a simple object literal with properties for 'name' and 'age'.
steps.hint: An object literal uses curly braces {} and contains key-value pairs separated by commas.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have an object with name and age properties that can store data.
successCriteria: An object literal with 'name' and 'age' properties is created.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your object has both 'name' and 'age' properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try creating an object literal using curly braces {} with properties for name and age.

steps.title: Access and modify object properties
steps.instruction: Access the 'name' property of your object using dot notation and log it to the console.
steps.hint: Use console.log() with your object's name followed by .propertyName.
steps.seedCode:
// Create your object literal here

// Access and log the 'name' property
steps.expectedOutcome: The console will display the value of the 'name' property from your object.
successCriteria: The 'name' property is accessed using dot notation
The value is logged to the console
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using dot notation (object.property) and logging the result.
steps.feedbackWrong: Use dot notation to access the 'name' property and log it with console.log().

steps.title: Add methods to an object
steps.instruction: Add a method to your object that returns a formatted string combining the object's properties.
steps.hint: Define a function as a property of your object. The function should use 'this' to access the object's other properties and return a string.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your object will have a method that can be called to return a string containing the object's property values.
successCriteria: The object has a method defined as a property that returns a formatted string using 'this' to reference other properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a method, but make sure it returns a formatted string that includes the object's properties using 'this'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The method wasn't added correctly. Remember to define a function as a property of your object that returns a string combining its properties.

steps.title: Create multiple objects with constructor function
steps.instruction: Create a constructor function named 'Person' that takes 'name' and 'age' parameters and assigns them as properties to the created object.
steps.hint: Define a function that uses 'this' to set properties when called with 'new'.
steps.expectedOutcome: A constructor function that can create multiple Person objects with name and age properties.
successCriteria: The Person constructor function is defined with name and age parameters, and uses 'this' to assign them as properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function takes both name and age parameters and assigns them using 'this'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try creating a function named Person that sets this.name and this.age from the parameters.

steps.title: Add methods via constructor prototype
steps.instruction: Add a method called 'getFullName' to the Person constructor's prototype that returns the person's full name by combining the 'firstName' and 'lastName' properties.
steps.hint: You can add a method to the prototype using Person.prototype.methodName = function() { ... }.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Person constructor now has a prototype method 'getFullName' that can be called on any Person instance.
successCriteria: The Person.prototype has a 'getFullName' method that returns a string combining firstName and lastName.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're adding the method to Person.prototype and that it correctly uses 'this.firstName' and 'this.lastName'.
steps.feedbackWrong: add the method to Person.prototype so all instances can access it.

steps.title: Create objects using Object.create()
steps.instruction: Create a new object named 'student' using Object.create() with the Person prototype as its prototype.
steps.hint: Use Object.create() and pass the Person.prototype as the argument to create an object that inherits from Person.
steps.expectedOutcome: The student object will be created with Person.prototype as its prototype, enabling inheritance of Person methods.
successCriteria: The student object is created using Object.create(Person.prototype).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using Object.create() and passing Person.prototype as the argument.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. You need to create a student object using Object.create(Person.prototype).

steps.title: Check prototype relationships
steps.instruction: Add code to check if the student object is an instance of the Person constructor using instanceof.
steps.hint: Use the instanceof operator with the student object and Person constructor.
steps.expectedOutcome: The code will verify the prototype relationship between the student object and Person constructor.
successCriteria: The instanceof operator is used to check if student is an instance of Person.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using the instanceof operator with the student object and Person constructor.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try using the instanceof operator to check if student is an instance of Person.

steps.title: Define a class with constructor
steps.instruction: Create a class named 'Car' with a constructor that takes 'brand' and 'year' parameters and assigns them to instance properties.
steps.hint: Use the 'class' keyword followed by the class name, then define a constructor method inside that accepts parameters and sets 'this.brand' and 'this.year'.
steps.expectedOutcome: A class named Car is defined with a constructor that initializes brand and year properties.
successCriteria: The Car class is defined with a constructor that sets this.brand and this.year based on parameters.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your class is named 'Car' and the constructor properly assigns both 'brand' and 'year' parameters to instance properties using 'this'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The class definition is missing or incorrect. Remember to use the 'class' keyword, define a constructor method, and assign parameters to instance properties with 'this'.

steps.title: Add instance methods to a class
steps.instruction: Add a method named 'honk' to your Car class that returns a string containing the car's brand and model.
steps.hint: Define the method inside the class body, using the same syntax as the constructor but without the 'constructor' keyword.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Car class should have a honk method that returns a string using the instance's brand and model properties.
successCriteria: The Car class includes a honk method that returns a string containing the car's brand and model.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a method, but make sure it returns a string that includes both the brand and model properties from the instance.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Car class doesn't have a honk method that returns the expected string. Check that the method is defined inside the class body and uses the instance properties.

steps.title: Add static methods to a class
steps.instruction: Add a static method called 'info' to your Car class that returns a string describing the class purpose.
steps.hint: Use the 'static' keyword before the method name inside the class definition. The method should return a string like 'This is a Car class for creating vehicle objects.'
steps.expectedOutcome: The Car class will have a static method that can be called directly on the class (Car.info()) without creating an instance.
successCriteria: The Car class contains a static method named 'info' that returns a string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the 'static' keyword and the method returns a string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The static method wasn't added correctly. Remember to use the 'static' keyword before the method name inside the class definition.

steps.title: Create a subclass with inheritance
steps.instruction: Create a subclass named ElectricCar that extends your existing Car class. Add a constructor that takes make, model, and batteryCapacity parameters, calls super with make and model, and sets this.batteryCapacity to batteryCapacity.
steps.hint: Use the 'extends' keyword to inherit from Car. In the constructor, call super(make, model) before setting the new property.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have an ElectricCar class that inherits from Car and adds a batteryCapacity property.
successCriteria: ElectricCar class is defined with extends Car, constructor calls super with make and model, and sets this.batteryCapacity.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure ElectricCar extends Car, the constructor calls super with make and model, and sets this.batteryCapacity.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a class named ElectricCar that extends Car, with a constructor that takes make, model, and batteryCapacity, calls super, and sets the batteryCapacity property.

steps.title: Override methods in a subclass
steps.instruction: In your ElectricCar subclass, override the honk method to return a different message.
steps.hint: Define a honk method inside the ElectricCar class that returns a string like 'Beep beep - electric!'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ElectricCar subclass should have its own honk method that returns a different string than the parent Car class's honk method.
successCriteria: ElectricCar has a honk method that returns a string different from Car's honk method.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the honk method in ElectricCar returns a different string than the one in Car.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ElectricCar subclass should have its own honk method that returns a different message than the parent Car class.
